title: Ashwin Reveals Why He Barely Spoke to Sanjay Manjrekar for Years After Fitness Criticism
excerpt: The retired off-spinner said Manjrekar's remarks about his fitness after the 2014-15 Australia tour made him angry and hurt, leading to years of silence between the two.
body:
• Ravichandran Ashwin revealed that Sanjay Manjrekar's criticism of his fitness after India's 2014-15 Australia tour left him deeply hurt and angry.
  • The retired off-spinner admitted he barely spoke to the commentator for years after what he felt was an unfair personal attack.
  • Ashwin said a 2015 article by Manjrekar helped repair the relationship, and the two eventually reconciled.
  • The revelation sheds light on the emotional toll media criticism takes on elite cricketers, even those with 537 Test wickets.

Ravichandran Ashwin has opened up about why he stopped talking to commentator Sanjay Manjrekar for years, revealing that the former India batter's criticism of his fitness after the 2014-15 Australia tour cut deep enough to sever communication between the two for an extended period.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin — who retired from international cricket in December 2024 with 537 Test wickets — said the criticism went beyond what he considered fair cricketing assessment and felt personal. "I got angry, felt very bad," Ashwin said, according to Hindustan Times.

The Criticism That Stung

India's tour of Australia in 2014-15 was a difficult one for the team, which lost the Test series 2-0. Ashwin, then still establishing himself as India's premier spinner, came under scrutiny for his fitness and performances in conditions that offered little assistance to slow bowlers.

Manjrekar, who has built a reputation for blunt commentary, criticized Ashwin's fitness levels following the tour. For Ashwin, that crossed a line. The off-spinner felt the critique was not about his bowling skills or tactical acumen but a personal attack on his physical conditioning — territory he considered off-limits for fair cricketing discourse.

"I got angry, felt very bad. I barely spoke to him for years after that."

— Ravichandran Ashwin, on his YouTube channel

The revelation adds a deeply personal chapter to the well-documented tension between Ashwin and Manjrekar. The commentator has been a persistent critic of Ashwin's career, previously questioning whether the off-spinner deserved the tag of an "all-time great" due to his relatively modest record in SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand, and Australia).

How a 2015 Article Changed Things

Ashwin indicated that the frosty relationship thawed after Manjrekar published an article in 2015 that the spinner felt was more balanced and fair. The piece apparently offered a more nuanced assessment of Ashwin's abilities, and it opened a door for reconciliation between the two Tamil Nadu cricketers.

The off-spinner has previously acknowledged that while Manjrekar "criticised me throughout my career," he has "never held any grudge against him" — provided the criticism stays within the bounds of on-field performance. "What they say might be right or wrong, as long as the criticism doesn't get personal, I am fine with it," Ashwin said last year while defending young pacer Harshit Rana from similar media pile-ons.

A Pattern of Tension

The Ashwin-Manjrekar dynamic has produced several public flashpoints over the years. In 2021, Manjrekar declared on ESPNcricinfo that he did not consider Ashwin an all-time great because the spinner lacked a five-wicket haul in SENA countries. Ashwin responded with a cheeky Tamil movie meme on social media.

More recently, in June 2026, the pair clashed again — this time over teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Manjrekar suggested the youngster should be dropped from the India A side after a physical altercation during a Tri-Series match in Sri Lanka. Ashwin fired back, questioning why critics were "invested in attacking him rather than guiding him" and drawing a sharp distinction between constructive criticism and hatred.

The Bigger Picture for Indian Cricket

Ashwin's candid admission speaks to a broader tension in Indian cricket between players and the commentary establishment. With retired cricketers increasingly building media careers on YouTube channels and television, the line between expert analysis and personal criticism has blurred.

For the Indian diaspora, which follows cricket with an intensity that rivals any domestic fanbase, the Ashwin-Manjrekar saga is more than gossip. It raises questions about how the media ecosystem around Indian cricket treats its greatest players — and whether the culture of sharp-tongued punditry, which generates clicks and views, comes at a cost to the athletes themselves.

Ashwin retired as India's second-highest wicket-taker in Test cricket, behind only Anil Kumble's 619. His 537 wickets came across 106 Tests at an average of 24.00, a record that speaks for itself regardless of what any commentator thinks of his fitness levels.
nri_angle: The Ashwin-Manjrekar saga highlights how the Indian cricket media ecosystem, closely followed by the global diaspora, handles criticism of elite players.
